title: Ocasio-Cortez Transfers $1 Million to El-Sayed in Michigan Senate Race's Final Sprint
excerpt: The New York congresswoman campaigned through Michigan's Republican-leaning Upper Peninsula as both parties pour resources into the open seat that may decide control of the Senate.
body:
• Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez transferred $1 million on Friday to a political account backing Dr. Abdul El-Sayed's Senate campaign in Michigan — an unusually large sum for a House member to send into another state's race.
  • She spent Thursday campaigning with El-Sayed across Michigan's Upper Peninsula, Republican-leaning territory where one county, Delta, voted for Donald Trump 64–34 in 2024.
  • The open seat, vacated by retiring Sen. Gary Peters, is Republicans' best Senate pickup chance: no Republican has won a Michigan Senate race since 1994, and losing it would force Democrats to flip five other GOP-held seats for a majority.
  • Vice President JD Vance has called the Michigan race the most important in the country and rallied for Republican Mike Rogers; former President Barack Obama campaigns for El-Sayed in Detroit on October 24.

Michigan's Senate race has become the midterms' marquee fight, and its final stretch now has a price tag to match: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has transferred $1 million to help elect Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, the progressive Democratic nominee, according to the New York Times. The transfer, made on Friday, is an exceptional move for a House member into a Senate race in another state, and it underlines how much of Ocasio-Cortez's own national future — she is considering a 2028 presidential run — she has staked on the result.

"I'm not waking up on November 4th wishing I did more to combat the smears aimed at Abdul. I'm leaving everything I can on the field."

— Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez

Campaigning where Democrats rarely go

The money followed a day of retail campaigning in the Upper Peninsula, as the Detroit Free Press reported: three stops including Escanaba, where about 500 people packed a fairground pavilion in a county Donald Trump carried by 30 points. El-Sayed, a physician and former Detroit health official, pitched cost-of-living politics rather than primary-season progressivism, urging supporters to talk to Trump voters in their own lives. Ocasio-Cortez and Sen. Bernie Sanders had campaigned for him before the August primary; she told the crowd El-Sayed had "built a winning coalition with an agenda to bring down costs for Michigan families."

https://x.com/OccupyDemocrats/status/2111132843489595731

Why this seat decides the Senate

The arithmetic is stark. The seat is open because Sen. Gary Peters is retiring. Republicans have not won a Michigan Senate race since 1994, which makes this their single best pickup opportunity of the cycle. Hold Michigan and Democrats' path to a majority stays plausible; lose it and they must flip five additional Republican-held seats. Vice President Vance, rallying in Monroe for Trump-backed Republican Mike Rogers, called it the most important contest in the country. Former President Obama joins El-Sayed and gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson in Detroit on October 24.

The diaspora dimension

El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, would be among the Senate's first Muslim members, and the race runs through metro Detroit's Arab American and South Asian communities — among the largest immigrant constituencies in any swing state. For Indian American voters in Michigan, many of whom share the cost, healthcare and immigration concerns at the centre of his campaign, the contest is a test of whether immigrant-background candidates can carry a statewide ticket in a presidential battleground. Election Day is November 3; the result will be known, as Ocasio-Cortez put it, by the morning of November 4.
